topic: Benjamin-Plus Review 2026: A Measured Token-Efficiency Skill for Coding Agents

key_points: Primary/authoritative source. Benjamin-Plus is a token-efficiency skill for coding agents by JetBrains, MIT licensed, released Aug 17 2026, ~270-540 stars.
Core claim: changes how the agent looks things up and waits, never what it builds. Measured up to −18% cost and −22% tokens per task, quality unchanged.

Five habits: (1) recon in one pass, (2) keyhole reads (~50 lines not whole file; transformed data never truncated), (3) probe environment once, (4) green means the task's own check = definition of done, stop when it passes, (5) polling is a step (check every 30s not every second).
Install method finding: injected saves (−17.9% cost median); as a discoverable skill folder saves nothing (−0.5% n.s., agents burned steps finding SKILL.md). Distribute via hooks/injection only.
Injected payload ~745 tokens (RULESET.md, ~3KB injected-instruction.md).

v6 FINAL (2026-08-16) on 80 paired SkillsBench tasks (Sonnet 5, low effort, Claude Code 2.1.201): cost −17.9% median paired (p=0.005), −16.7% totals; turns −20.0% (p=0.001); total tokens −21.9% (p=0.001); cache reads −23.9%; output −21.2%; code written −13.3%; wall-clock −15.6%.
Quality: no difference detected (7 better / 5 worse / 68 tie, sign p=0.77; mean reward 0.362→0.392), not powered as equivalence test.

Honesty note: v5 same-day run measured −10.0% median cost (p=0.169, not significant); control arm drifted +10.5% between days while treatment stayed flat. Skill acts as a session-cost variance clamp; floor ~−10% cheap-baseline day, ~−18% against bloated baseline.
v6 added 'Polling is a step' rule from Java SWE-bench traces: 45.8% of treated-arm steps were polls, 3,982 at sub-5s yields.

Install-method external result (Java SWE-bench, Codex CLI, 225×3 replicas): hook-injected −4.4% cost [−7.5,−1.5] p=0.003, solve rate unchanged p=0.22, tool calls −20%; skill-folder + fetching SKILL.md cost median 3 steps with 73% path misses → −0.5% n.s. Program spend ~$153 across 254 billed trials.
Community indexing entry (Cult of Claude). Lists repo with 272 stars, first seen 2026-08-27, category Development, type community, author JetBrains.
Install guidance matches repo: copy folder into ~/.claude/skills/ or file into ~/.claude/agents/.
Related context: Budget (token-efficiency audits) and Financial Controller agents show the broader token/spend-management tool ecosystem around coding agents.
AI tool directory entry: 'instruction-set skill' that reduces token and tool-call usage without changing the agent's implementation task.

Teaches five operating habits (recap): batch repo reconnaissance into one pass, inspect narrow file windows unless full data needed, probe dependencies in one command, treat task's verification command as definition of done, poll unfinished builds at longer intervals.

Intended to be injected into agent instructions rather than installed as a discoverable skill; provides injected-instruction files for Claude Code hooks, Codex AGENTS.md, project CLAUDE.md, or system prompts.
Reports ~10%–18% cost reduction depending on baseline, unchanged quality.

JetBrains' wider context: series benchmarking public 'token saver' add-ons with the same paired-A/B method. Part 1 caveman (advertised −65%, measured −8.5%); Part 2 rtk (advertised −60–90%, measured +7.6%); Part 3 Ponytail (advertised −54%, measured in detail).
Same discipline Benjamin-Plus follows: measure against a baseline rather than trust vendor claims — many advertised token-saver skills underperform or outright increase cost.
Separate JetBrains eval: giving agents IDE-native search tools got them faster and cheaper (total cost −4.07% to −13.48% across GPT 5.4 Java/Kotlin and Codex 5.2).
Korean-Japanese trend analysis: AI coding differentiation shifting from 'models' to 'skill design'; benchmark-driven skill engineering emerging on GitHub.
Frames Benjamin-Plus (Aug 2026, MIT) as the 'hidden gem' measuring 'agent waste'; paired-A/B verifies skills that reduce token cost while maintaining quality.
Contrast with Autoprompt (73/89 vs 60/89 Terminal-Bench successes, but notes tokens may double / time triple, unlogged).

Thesis: agent skills evolving from 'collections of convenient prompts' into engineering assets measured and improved with evidence; 'skill evaluation' may become an independent layer beside Model, Harness, Memory.
Long agent traces show 'small waste' accumulates in conversation context and gets re-read every turn — the economic rationale for keyhole reads and batching.

stats.fact: Benjamin-Plus advertised ceiling: up to −18% cost and −22% tokens per task with quality unchanged.
v6 FINAL (80 paired SkillsBench, Sonnet 5, Claude Code 2.1.201): cost −17.9% median paired (p=0.005), −16.7% totals; median cost saving statistically solid.
Same eval: turns −20.0% (p=0.001), total tokens −21.9% (p=0.001), cache reads −23.9%, output tokens −21.2%, code written −13.3%, wall-clock −15.6%.
Quality unchanged: 7 better / 5 worse / 68 ties (sign p=0.77); Verifier mean reward 0.362→0.392 — not powered as an equivalence test.
Install method matters: injected saves −17.9% cost median; as a discoverable skill folder saves nothing (−0.5% n.s.) because agents burned ~3 steps with 73% path misses finding SKILL.md.
Cross-platform replication: Java SWE-bench (Codex CLI, gpt-5.6-luna, 675 paired replicas) hook-injected skill measured −4.4% cost [−7.5,−1.5] p=0.003, solve rate unchanged (p=0.22), tool calls −20%.

Skill acts as a session-cost variance clamp: v5 measured −10.0% median cost (p=0.169, not significant); control baseline drifted +10.5% between days while treated arm stayed flat (−3.0%). Floor ~−10%, up to ~−18% against a bloated baseline.
'Polling is a step' rule added after Java SWE-bench traces showed 45.8% of the treated arm's agent steps were polls, 3,982 of them at sub-5s yields.
Injected payload is small: ~745 tokens (RULESET.md); full injected-instruction.md is ~3KB to append to system prompt/AGENTS.md.
Benchmark program spend: ~$153 across 254 billed trials to develop and validate the skill via iterative paired A/B.
Context: other advertised token-saver skills often underperform — caveman claimed −65% (measured −8.5%), rtk claimed −60–90% (measured +7.6%).
Repository traction (2026-09): ~311 stars / 13 forks per gitstars; Cult of Claude lists it with 272 stars, first seen 2026-08-27.

angles: Measured, not marketed: unlike caveman/rtk 'token saver' skills whose claims don't survive A/B, Benjamin-Plus publishes the full paired-A/B methodology (80 SkillsBench + 675 Java SWE-bench replicas) and honest caveats in EXPECTED-RESULTS.md.

Inject, don't install: the decisive finding is distribution method — injection into session/system prompts saves, discoverable skill folders don't (SKILL.md discovery costs steps). Practical setup guide for Claude Code hooks and Codex AGENTS.md.
The five habits as an economic theory of agent waste: every clumsy lookup is paid twice (the step + every re-read in growing context); keyhole reads and batching attack the compounding context cost.
Benjamin-Plus as a session-cost variance clamp: works hardest when baseline sessions are bloated (~−18%); modest (~−10%) on already-lean baselines — calibrate expectations.
Bigger trend: benchmark-driven skill engineering — shifting competition from model choice to skill design; 'Skill Evaluation' emerging as an independent layer beside Model, Harness, Memory.
Quality-preserving frugality: the sign test (7 better / 5 worse / 68 tie) shows cost savings with no detectable quality loss — a rare 'free lunch' claim that survives measurement.
Practical adoption checklist for teams running Claude Code/Codex/Cursor: inject payload, verify via /hooks, watch tool-call counts and polling steps in traces.
